summary.headline: Advit Jewels FY26 revenue rose 33.68% to INR 167.03 crore and net profit 35.56% to INR 34.39 crore, but Q4 was softer at INR 43.23 crore income.
summary.overview: FY26 was the company's strongest year: total income grew 33.68% to INR 1,67,02,56,000, EBITDA rose 32.52% to INR 49,23,80,000 at a 29.48% margin, and net profit grew 35.56% to INR 34,38,79,000. Q4 FY26 was weaker year-on-year, with total income of INR 43,22,92,000, EBITDA of INR 12,55,56,000 (29.04% margin) and net profit of INR 8,74,05,000 (diluted EPS INR 2.79). Management attributed the Q4 softness to luxury demand being hit by the January-March war escalation, and said December-booked orders were executed in the quarter. The company listed on NSE and BSE during the year and is moving toward retail stores and exports.

segments.name: Bridal and Polki jewellery (core)
segments.commentary: Management said the business is 100% Jadau Polki, with Kundan, Meena, Polki and antique bridal jewellery as the core; an analyst cited about 98% of revenue from these categories. Customer count rose from 96 to 274 in FY26.

segments.name: B2B vs B2C mix
segments.commentary: Management said the mix has moved to roughly 80:20, with B2C growing through word of mouth and roadshows after the IPO, though the split was described qualitatively.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports contributed less than 1% of FY26 revenue, per the analyst question; management said the export journey has not really started and cited one Instagram-sourced US sale.

demand_pricing: Management attributed Q4 softness to luxury demand being affected by the January-March war escalation, and said strong September-December orders were booked and executed.
Management said luxury bridal demand is expected to pick up from late November with NRI and wedding season, and that Diwali is not a luxury jewellery season.
Management cited an addressable Indian bridal Polki market of about INR 20,000 crore (1 lakh HNI weddings at roughly INR 20 lakh average ticket), with the company targeting about 1% share.
Management said margins are held by pricing for artwork and craftsmanship, and that Polki margins are comparable to big jewellers' Polki margins; gold-only jewellery margins are lower.
Average bridal set value cited at INR 60 lakh, with individual sets ranging from INR 20 lakh to INR 1 crore.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on brand, craftsmanship and long-term demand, but evasive on quantified items: gold share, FY27 targets, Q1 trends, store capex and payback were deflected or referred to the DRHP.

qa_highlights.question: Why did capacity utilisation fall to around 31% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said weight-based utilisation does not fit Polki and diamond jewellery; lighter gold weight was used in new products as gold prices rose, and turnover reflects stones and artwork value.

qa_highlights.question: Why did sales fall YoY in Q4 when peers reported strong growth, and what share of sales is gold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the January-March war escalation for luxury demand weakness and said December orders were executed in Q4; it declined to give a gold share, citing design-driven variation (e.g., a 30% gold illustrative piece).

qa_highlights.question: What are the planned store openings for FY27 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said at least three stores are targeted in FY27 with a franchise partner committed to 30 stores in three years; more details to come via new LOIs, and the Jaipur store targeted by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the addressable market and what are FY27 revenue and EBITDA targets, and how is Q1 shaping up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited an addressable Indian bridal Polki market of about INR 20,000 crore (1 lakh HNI weddings at INR 20 lakh), targeting 1% share; FY27 targets were referred to the DRHP and Q1 was described qualitatively only.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export roadmap and how many export sales came in?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exports have not really started; the one US sale came via Instagram, with the customer paying the 50% US tariff. Focus markets cited were UK (free trade, from 15 July) and Middle East shows.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins improve as the company shifts from B2B to B2C?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed margins should improve in direct-to-consumer sales, but said it would keep prices moderate to preserve the piece as a long-term asset for brides; B2B:B2C mix described as roughly 80:20.

guidance_outlook: No quantified FY27 revenue or EBITDA guidance given on the call; management referred to targets disclosed in the DRHP and to five-year projections on the company website.
Management said FY27 focus is on expanding customer network, new jewellery collections, manufacturing capabilities, operational efficiency and gradually strengthening international presence.

Store plan: at least three company-operated stores targeted in FY27 (per management, 'the target is minimum three'), with franchise partner committed to 30 stores in three years, to be rolled out cautiously.
Jaipur flagship store (~30,000 sq ft) targeted to open by end of calendar 2026; management said Diwali is not feasible and opening is tied to November-end NRI and wedding season.
Management said luxury bridal demand is expected to pick up from late November, and that new orders are expected from August.
Q1 FY27 trends were not quantified; management said existing business is 'anyway far better than our old' without numbers.
capex_capacity: Management did not give a capacity utilisation figure for FY26 beyond analyst's ~31% reference; it argued weight-based utilisation is not meaningful for Polki/diamond jewellery, and that lighter gold weight was used in new products as gold prices rose.
Jaipur retail store of around 30,000 sq ft under construction; interiors in progress, opening targeted by end of 2026; management said it would not open at 75-80% completion.
Store capex per outlet and payback period were not disclosed; management said these would be checked before rollout.
Designers: around seven to eight in-house designers; artisans being employed on year-round contracts rather than seasonal work.
New collections planned: men's Polki products (cufflinks, belt buckles, brooches, kilangi, rings) and lighter Gen Z jewellery; timing not specified beyond 'soon'.
risks_watch: Q4 FY26 total income fell YoY to INR 43.23 crore; management attributed it to war-related luxury demand weakness, and Q1 FY27 trends were not disclosed.
Quantified FY27 targets were deferred to the DRHP, leaving no near-term numerical benchmark for revenue or EBITDA.
Store rollout execution: Jaipur flagship timing (end-2026) slipped from Diwali; franchise commitment of 30 stores in three years is not yet firm and store capex and payback were not disclosed.
Concentration in bridal Polki (management said 100% Polki) and reliance on artisans, whose supply management said is constrained and is being addressed via year-round employment.
Export traction is minimal (<1% of FY26 revenue); monitor first UK and Middle East shows and any export conversions next quarter.
Gold share of sales and utilisation metrics were not disclosed; the 31% utilisation figure cited by an analyst was not reconciled by management.
key_quotes: Financial Year 26 was one of the strongest years in company's history.
So, why should I diversify my product portfolio? It is going so well.
